facts.big: have been to / has gone to
facts.label: Been to e gone to
facts.sub: Been to: foi e voltou (I have been to Chicago). Gone to: foi e ainda está lá (She has gone to the market). Pergunte Where have you been?

facts.label: Foi e voltou
facts.sub: Use have been to para lugares onde você foi e voltou: I have been to Chicago. A pessoa não está mais lá. Também serve para experiências: Have you ever been to Boston?

facts.label: Foi e está lá
facts.sub: Use has gone to quando a pessoa está lá agora ou a caminho: Jo has gone to the market. Ela não está aqui. Não use gone to para falar de você mesmo quando está presente.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Has been to means the person came back.
Has gone to means the person is back home.
items.why: It means the person is away.

items.s: “Where have you been?” asks about a recent place.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Has been to means the person came back. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Has gone to means the person is back home. → Falso (It means the person is away.)
“Where have you been?” asks about a recent place. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A walk on the street · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny Saturday on a quiet street in Denver. Mountains stand behind the houses like a blue wall. Kai waters the plants in front of his house. He sees his neighbor Eva with a big bag. She has just come back from a long trip. Kai waves and calls her name.

“Eva! Where have you been? I haven’t seen you for weeks.” says Kai. “I have been to Chicago to visit my cousins. I got back on Friday.” says Eva. “Nice! Have you been to the new market on Main Street?” says Kai.
